author: reek
body: The issue tracker's list view, moved out of `apps/guios/TrackerApp.codex` when the guios shell retired into GopDesk. The data layer moved with it as `GopTrackDb`, unchanged: it is a relational store over `DbServer` with no UI in it, which is why it survived the retirement while the four menu-item chapters did not.

author: reek
body: This is a real view over real rows. The issues are inserted into a catalog, queried back through the executor, filtered, and turned into table rows -- not a picture of a tracker.

author: reek
body: **What did NOT come across, and it is most of the old chapter.** The kanban board, the sprint-cycle dashboard, the detail overlay, the command palette and the focus ring were all built as `(GopBuf, ShellUiState)` painting through `gop-render-tree`, and every one of them needs UI state the shell owned. They are worth having and they are not lost -- the old chapter stays in the depot until they land -- but a pane that shows the issues is the rung that proves the data layer reaches the glass, and shipping the board half-wired would have proved less.

author: reek
body: Status and priority are stored as integers and rendered as words. The numbers are the database's and the words are this view's.

author: reek
body: Three filters: everything, open only, done only. Open excludes both Done and Cancelled, because an abandoned issue is not outstanding work.

author: reek
body: The row id is the index in the UNFILTERED result, so a row keeps its identity when the filter changes.
